rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked every pronoun/demonstrative/definite-noun across all 9 chunks in order. The pinned diff (43e6cae1..HEAD) only swaps 'Claude'->'the agent' at chunk 5 line 53, chunk 6 lines 60 and 62 — 'the agent' is training-register vocabulary (the training's own name is Agentic Engineering 101) already interchangeable with the 'Claude Code' / 'it' references established at chunk 1 line 22 and chunk 3 line 40; no referent broken by the swap. Closest-to-violating, unchanged by this diff: chunk 1 line 22 'The curated security skills install when you extract the bundle.' — 'the bundle' has no prior antecedent; the tarball is first named at chunk 4 line 45 (`ae101-content.tar.gz`) and 'the bundle' as a term first appears in chunk 5's own header (line 51), three slides later. Stays inside: the sentence's teaching point (skills install automatically at extraction, no separate step) does not depend on resolving what 'the bundle' specifically is, and this is the file's own established anticipatory-preview device, used twice already one paragraph earlier in the same chunk-0/chunk-1 span ('the repo picked', 'the curated skills installed' at line 7; 'the repo itself (picked next)' at line 22) before the reader ever meets 'the bundle' — a reader primed by two prior instances of the same device is not confused by a third. No other candidate: chunk 3 line 40 'the repo you just picked' resolves to chunk 2 (sequential); chunk 6 line 66 'the candidate-bug screen' resolves to chunk 6 line 62 'the bug screen' (in-chunk); chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked' resolves to chunk 6's bug-screen (same-file backward).

Two off-file links, both named not located: chunk 2 line 34 '[build one from zero](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/build-a-project-from-zero.md)' names the destination in the link text itself; chunk 7 line 76 'Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)' names author and title in the same sentence. Neither points at another file by position ('the opening lecture said'). The pinned diff (Claude->the agent swaps) sits outside both. No cross-file positional callback found anywhere in the body.

Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md --report` this session: thinnest chunk is '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' at 17 words, but it carries two self-standing instructions (fetch the tarball via the prompt; manual-download fallback link) — not a bare wait-state or context-dependent bullet. No orphan found across the 9 chunks.

Checked all 8 headers against their own chunk content. Closest-to-violating: chunk 4 '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' (line 43) — its content (line 45) only asks the student to fetch `ae101-content.tar.gz`, which becomes a folder only after chunk 5's extraction. Stays inside: nothing in the chunk contradicts the header — 'folder' names the well-understood eventual outcome of this download step in a two-step download+extract pair, and chunk 5's own header 'Extract the bundle' makes the split explicit; no false claim, only an anticipatory label. Every other header matches its content exactly, including the two chunks touched by the pinned diff (5, 6) where a wording swap did not change what either header promises.

Checked all 5 sub-items across all 9 chunks, including the 3 diff-touched lines (53, 60, 62 — plain 'Claude'->'the agent' noun swaps, no rhetorical shape changed): no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative; no number-plus-own-retraction (the runtime/time figures sit in the maintainer block, below the cut, out of body scope; the in-body '30 to 120 minutes' at line 18 is a plain estimate range, not a number followed by its own retraction); no abstraction-noun stack; no empty-leg verb triplet ('test, branch, commit, and open a PR' at line 60 is four distinct concrete actions, none vacuous). Clean across the file.

Two body hits on the bare word 'surface' (line 17 'user-facing surface', line 29 'surface area for rules and memory to land on') are ordinary engineering usage (attack-surface/API-surface family), not the repo's writing-surface-as-noun jargon — explicitly the carved-out sense. 'the agent' (lines 53, 60, 62, this diff's only change) and 'Session' widget label (line 38) are training-register/architecture-mandated, not repo-internal dialect. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped all body bold spans (`grep -n '\*\*'` over the raw source, lines 1-83): chunk 1 lines 15-18 carry one short (≤3-word) handle bold per bullet ('Trivial bug', 'A small multi-file task', 'A small feature', 'A bigger piece') distinguishing task-size entries a reader scans to find their own size — the reading-list/menu-slide waiver applies by function (a slide meant to be scanned for the reader's own entry point, not read straight through), each bold well under the ≲5-word handle cap. Chunk 3 line 38 '**Session**' is the architecture-mandated widget label (widgets.md), not narrative bold. Chunks 4-6's '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' labels do not exist as authored bold in the raw source at all — they are build-time chrome synthesised from the `{{prompt:<key>}}` marker by scripts/expand-md.js, confirmed against the raw body.txt (lines 47, 55, 64, 68 are bare markers, no literal `**`). Chunk 7 line 76 carries exactly one bolded element, '**Read:**' (1 word), leaving the title/author plain — the literal shape the compendium names as correct. No chunk exceeds its budget; the pinned diff does not touch a bold span.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 8 body headings are imperative ('Bring real work', 'Bring to Module 1') or numbered phase/step labels ('1. Pick THE repo' ... '5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') — the exercise-heading convention, matching what this file is (a task walkthrough, not a lecture). No slide here is a law/consolidation moment where the header IS the teaching, so the claim requirement never triggers. 'Pre-read before Module 1' and 'Bring to Module 1' read as the explicit NOT-violation carve-out (orientation/catalogue-style labels), not mislabelled claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all three classes against every bullet/sentence in all 9 chunks. (a) doctrine restatement — none found; prework has no prior lens/split/law to re-announce, it is pure logistics, and the 4 task-size bullets (chunk 1) and 3 repo-criteria bullets (chunk 2) each add a distinct move/object, not a recap. (b) self-referential design commentary — no sentence anywhere tells the student they are inside a pedagogy or names the curriculum's own design intent. (c) aphorism kicker — closest candidate chunk 6 line 70 '*Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there.*'; stays inside because it is concrete to the specific AskUserQuestion tip just given (lines 66-68), not a restatement of the header ('5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') or a `**The point:**`-style line. No bullet meeting the 'carries nothing' bar found.
